The '''auditor general of Canada''' (French: '''La vérificatrice générale du Canada'''{{efn| Is called ''Le vérificateur général du Canada'' when a man is holding the position}}) is a [[supreme audit institution]] which acts as an officer to the [[Parliament of Canada]] tasked with highlighting accountability and oversight by conducting independent financial audits of federal government's operations.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://lop.parl.ca/sites/PublicWebsite/default/en_CA/ResearchPublications/201171E |url-access= |title=The Office of the Auditor General of Canada: Beyond Bean Counting |last1=McGlashan |first1=Lindsay |author-link1= |date=9 July 2024 |orig-date=30 June 2011 |website=lop.parl.ca |series=Research Publication |publisher=Federal Parliament of Canada |agency=Library of Parliament |location=Ottawa, ON, CA |at=Parliament Hill |script-title= |trans-title= |type= |format= |arxiv= |asin= |bibcode= |doi= |isbn= |issn= |jfm= |jstor= |lccn= |mr= |oclc= |ol= |osti= |pmc= |pmid= |rfc= |ssrn= |zbl= |id= |access-date=31 October 2024 |url-status= |archive-url= |archive-date= |via= |quote= |trans-quote= }}</ref> These performance audits, known as the [[Auditor's report|Auditor-General's Report]], provide members of parliament with objective evidence to help them examine the government's activities and hold it to account and improve [[good governance]] among public officers included.

[[Karen Hogan]] was appointed Auditor General of Canada in June 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.intosaijournal.org/journal-entry/karen-hogan-appointed-auditor-general-canada/ |url-access= |title=Q3: Karen Hogan Appointed Auditor General of Canada |author=Staff writer |year=2020 |department=News In Brief |website=www.intosaijournal.org/author/intosai/ |series=International Journal of Government Auditing (the Journal) |publisher=International Organization of Supreme Audit Institutions (INTOSAI) |script-title= |trans-title= |type= |format= |arxiv= |asin= |bibcode= |doi= |isbn= |issn= |jfm= |jstor= |lccn= |mr= |oclc= |ol= |osti= |pmc= |pmid= |rfc= |ssrn= |zbl= |id= |access-date=31 October 2024 |url-status= |archive-url= |archive-date= |via= |quote= |trans-quote= }}</ref>  She replaced interim Auditor General of Canada Sylvain Ricard.<ref name="Government of Canada">{{Cite web|last=Government of Canada|first=Office of the Auditor General of Canada|date=2007-11-15|title=Who We Are|url=https://www.oag-bvg.gc.ca/internet/English/au_fs_e_370.html#AG_Canada|access-date=2020-07-21|website=www.oag-bvg.gc.ca}}</ref>

== Office ==
Auditors general are appointed by the [[Governor General of Canada|governor general]] in council ([[Cabinet of Canada|cabinet]]) on advice of the [[House of Commons of Canada|House of Commons]] and [[Senate of Canada|Senate]] for a non-renewable term of ten years. An auditor general may only be removed for cause by the [[King-in-Council|governor-in-council]] with the approval of both the House of Commons and [[Senate of Canada|Senate]]. The Oversight and Accountability (the [[Federal Accountability Act]]) and Auditor General Act gives this body substantial independence from both [[Cabinet (government)|cabinet]] and Head of Government control.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.statutes.ca/r-s-c-1985-c-a-17|title=Auditor General Act|accessdate=2025-06-10}}</ref>

The auditor general's responsibilities include:

* auditing operations of the federal and territorial governments
* providing Parliament and the legislative assemblies with independent information, assurance, and advice regarding the stewardship of public funds<ref name="Government of Canada"/>

On November 4, 2011, the [[Stephen Harper|prime minister]] appointed [[Michael Ferguson (Auditor General)|Michael Ferguson]], former auditor general of the province of [[New Brunswick]], as Auditor General of Canada, effective November 28, 2011. Sylvain Ricard, having been previously the deputy auditor general, was appointed by Prime Minister [[Justin Trudeau]] on March 29, 2019, to serve until a permanent replacement was selected.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Office|first=Prime Minister's|title=Prime Minister appoints interim Auditor General of Canada|url=https://www.newswire.ca/news-releases/prime-minister-appoints-interim-auditor-general-of-canada-824514740.html|access-date=2019-04-05|website=www.newswire.ca|language=en}}</ref>

The Office of the Auditor General of Canada was named one of "[[Canada's Top 100 Employers]]" by Mediacorp Canada Inc. five years in a row (2008–2012), and was featured in ''[[Maclean's]]'' news magazine.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eluta.ca/top-employer-auditor-general|title=Reasons for Selection, 2009 Canada's Top 100 Employers Competition}}</ref>

The commissioner of the environment and sustainable development, was created by Parliament in 1995 as an aide to the AGC, and has offices within the precinct of the AGC.  The commissioner is empowered under the 1995 amendments to the Auditor-General Act to receive "petitions on environmental and sustainable development matters and [to] require ministers to respond to them".<ref name="petitions">[http://www.oag-bvg.gc.ca/internet/English/pet_lp_e_930.html Backgrounder on powers of the Commissioner of the Environment and Sustainable Development]</ref>  The petition process requires the ministry to respond in 120 days, although the process may be delayed by litigation.<ref name="petitions"/>

The Office of the Auditor General of Canada is located in the [[C.D. Howe Building]] in [[Ottawa]].

The role of auditor general was introduced in 1878 and prior to the creation it was the head of the audit board (1867–1878).

In 1971, the auditor general's office hosted VII [[International Congress of Supreme Audit Institutions|INCOSAI]], the seventh triennial convention of the [[International Organization of Supreme Audit Institutions]].<ref>{{Cite book
  | title = [[:File:INTOSAI 50 Years.pdf|INTOSAI: 50 Years (1953-2003)]]
  | publisher = [[International Organization of Supreme Audit Institutions]]
  | year = 2004
  | location = [[Vienna, Austria|Vienna]]
  | page = 51}}</ref>

The Auditor General Act underpins the office as an independent official.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2011-05-25 |title=Sheila Fraser: Her greatest hits |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/sheila-fraser-her-greatest-hits-1.1066311 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160710064845/https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/sheila-fraser-her-greatest-hits-1.1066311 |archive-date=2016-07-10 |access-date=2025-05-18 |work=CBC News}}</ref>
